newsitem.title: UK: Nigerian spot oil values slide further, losses mount.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian spot oil values slide further, losses mount.

text.p: Lifters of Nigerian crude oil on Friday were facing mounting losses worth millions of dollars as spot market values tumbled further and the state marketer decided against revising contract prices.

"It's about as bad as we can remember," said a trader for a major Nigerian equity holder of the gap between spot market values and contract prices. "Forcados is being talked around (Dated Brent) minus 30 cents a barrel," he added.
Forcados, one of the two main Nigerian crude streams, was priced by state Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) at benchmark Dated Brent +47 cents for cargoes loading in March.

Even at a 20-cent discount to Dated Brent, the sale of a March loading 950,000-barrel distillate-rich Forcados cargo on the spot market would cost the contract holder more than half a million dollars.
About half a dozen March cargoes remained unsold, in part the legacy of slack demand for heating oil at the tail end of a relatively mild winter in the United States, traders said.

A heavy programme of refinery maintenance on the east coast of the U.S., the single biggest consumer of Nigerian crude, the resumption of limited exports by Iraq and inflated Dated Brent quotes -- which restricted arbitrage options -- all helped build the overhang.

"There has been less moving to the Far East this month partly because of ample stocks of Indonesian crude but also because while the Brent/Dubai spread was working, Dated was pretty strong," said a trader.
Contract holders said they were not surprised at NNPC's decision not to revise March prices. "Think how much they would have had to cut by just to ease the pain," said one.
"They have kept to the usual policy of sticking it out and making life easier for the lifters later in the year," he added.
NNPC normally seeks to set crude contract prices at about 11 cents below spot market values to cover business costs and profits.
NNPC said on Friday that it hoped margins on average this year for Nigerian crude contract holders would at least match those in 1996.
Spot market weakness was not limited to distillate-rich Forcados, traders said on Friday.
Grades like Bonny Light, Qua Iboe and Brass River, typically sought after in the spring and summer because of higher gasoline yields, were also suffering under the weight of about 10 unsold stems.
Bonny Light was assessed by several traders at around Dated Brent +25 cents for March cargoes, around 33 cents a barrel adrift from its March contract price.
One lifter valued it as low as "the high teens" above Dated, while others said early April barrels would be worth nearer Dated Brent +40 cents.
"The prompter cargoes are certainly under the greatest pressure," said one.
"You have to remember that even the lights still produce a lot of gas oil," said another.
Brass River was offered at Dated Brent +40 cents, off 15 cents from mid-week values.
Nigeria sells some 850,000 bpd of crude through contracts with traders and refiners, adjusting prices every month according to NNPC's assessment of the spot market.
--Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
